clue.text: It may be tugged to get cabbage back into cleft

indicators.note: into says the turned cabbage word is placed inside the word for cleft

parts.note: a fork is a cleft or split, as in a fork in a road

indicators.note: back tells us the cabbage word is read from right to left

parts.note: cole is an old name for cabbage, as in coleslaw

explanation.surface: A gardener tugs at something to wrench a cabbage back into a split in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses COLE to give ELOC. Tugging the forelock is the old gesture of deference to a social superior, so 'It may be tugged' is a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuft of hair over the brow was traditionally pulled as a mark of respect, hence something tugged.

indicators.note: dropping says the letter for name is let fall from the business word

parts.note: finance is money matters, the business of handling funds

explanation.surface: Someone devoted to name-dropping in the world of commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name-dropping' looks like the social vice, but it splits: N (name) is dropped from FINANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone engaged to be married has made a commitment to their future spouse.

indicators.note: involving means the ceremony word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the runner-up word is removed

parts.note: the runner-up comes second

explanation.surface: A mysterious ritual in which the person who came second appears without a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops the first letter, leaving ECOND, and 'involving' puts that inside the ceremony word.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite knowledge is obscure and little known, the same quality as arcane lore.

clue.text: Free association, subsequently, with the Arabic spare ruler

parts.note: later means subsequently
al is the Arabic word for the, as in Al-Qaeda
spare can mean lean or thin, as in a spare frame
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Musing freely about an Arab monarch with no heir to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare' here is the adjective meaning lean, not extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral thinking means tackling problems by unconventional, freely associated ideas rather than step-by-step logic.

indicators.note: kept means the villa word holds the quiet letter inside it

parts.note: a chalet is a type of villa or holiday house; the 's stands for has
P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A garland of flowers has been kept quiet by the owner of a villa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garland's' is read as 'garland is', so the definition takes the 's as a link to the wordplay. 'kept' puts P inside CHALET.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a wreath or circlet of flowers worn on the head, a kind of garland.

indicators.note: takes means the snake word holds the shelter word inside it

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
lee means shelter, the side protected from the wind

explanation.surface: A sleeping snake has found somewhere sheltered to lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant is inactive as if sleeping, like a hibernating animal.

clue.text: Vice shelter to hand out charity

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A refuge for vice gives handouts to the needy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges VICE SHELTER plus HAND, with 'to' a link joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: Save the Children is a well-known international charity working for young people's welfare.

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the beat word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cane is to beat

explanation.surface: A drummer sets the time before beating it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat up' looks like a phrase meaning attack, but 'up' reverses the beat word to give ENAC.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact a law is to establish it formally by legislation.

clue.text: Far too much to God in prayer

indicators.note: in tells us the god's name sits inside the prayer word

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request, a prayer
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: Someone offers far too much to God in their prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link; the surface makes 'God' look like the addressee of the prayer, but he is inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excess or overabundance of something.

indicators.note: cracked suggests something broken apart, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An elderly man has broken open a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' rearranges the letters of OLD MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An almond is an edible kernel, a type of nut.

clue.text: Sporting venue for A. Murray, say

parts.note: Andy Murray, the tennis player, is a Scot

explanation.surface: Asking where a famous tennis player might compete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A. Murray' looks like Andy Murray as a whole, but A stays as written and Murray is an example of a Scot. ASCOT is a racecourse in Berkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English racecourse, host of Royal Ascot, so a sporting venue.

clue.text: Fitzgerald makes comeback — ruining Evita with ease!

indicators.note: makes comeback means the singer's name is turned round to run backwards

parts.note: Ella Fitzgerald was a famous jazz singer

indicators.note: ruining means the letters of Evita are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A jazz star returns to the stage and wrecks a performance of a musical with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes comeback' turns ELLA into ALLE; 'ruining' shuffles EVITA into VIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate pain is to relieve or lessen it, the verb sense of ease.

clue.text: Fuel carrying books right to singer

indicators.note: carrying means the fuel word holds the books and right pieces inside it

parts.note: coal is a fuel
NT is the New Testament, books of the Bible
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fuel delivery includes books meant for a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: NT is the usual crossword abbreviation for the New Testament, hence 'books'.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is a female singer with the lowest voice range.

indicators.note: origin of means only the opening letter of the referenced word is used

parts.note: 22 refers to the answer of 22 across, a giant figure
an itch is a desire, as in an itch to travel

explanation.surface: A small person says where a giant's yearning comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: '22' points to 22 across; its first letter T is followed by ITCH. TITCH is British slang for a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: Titch is British informal slang for a very small person, a tiddler or shorty.

parts.note: fille is French for girl

explanation.surface: A girl overseas orders a T-bone steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T-bone' reads as a steak, but splits: T is the letter and 'bone' (as a verb) is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To fillet a fish is to remove its bones, so the verb means bone.

parts.note: an edger is one who edges, moving slowly and creepingly

explanation.surface: A ship's doctor has been given a climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship's' is read as 'ship is'; 'creeper' looks like a plant but is one who edges along.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredger is a vessel that scoops mud from the bottom of harbours and rivers.

indicators.note: borne means carried, so the wind word carries the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
a van is a vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vehicle is lifted by the wind and sent flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind-borne' reads as carried by the wind; here the wind word literally carries the other pieces inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To galvanise someone is to shock or stir them into action.

clue.text: Impediment to beheaded aristocrat eating catsup?

indicators.note: eating means the shortened aristocrat word takes the other piece inside it
beheaded means the first letter of the aristocrat word is cut off

parts.note: a noble is an aristocrat
read as cats up: the word cats written upwards, as in a down clue

explanation.surface: A headless nobleman is caught eating tomato ketchup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catsup' is an American spelling of ketchup, but it splits as CATS read up. 'beheaded' leaves OBLE, which 'eating' wraps round the reversed cats.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is something that blocks progress, a hindrance.

clue.text: Bloke's beginning to allow woman to rattle on

indicators.note: beginning means only the first letter of the bloke word is taken

parts.note: to let is to allow
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A man starts letting a woman talk on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: BLETHER is a Scottish word for idle chatter or to talk nonsense at length.
explanation.definitionFit: To blether is to chatter foolishly and at length, Scots for prattle.

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
a coil is a twist or spiral

explanation.surface: A dance kick from the hit song Let's Twist Again.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse clue order: RE from 'Again' then COIL from 'Twist'.
explanation.definitionFit: The recoil of a gun is its kick when fired.

parts.note: a call to look, as in lo and look there, and a question inviting the reader to see something

explanation.definitionFit: An archaic command meaning look or observe, said to make someone notice a sight.

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A recipe for cooking five viable shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a clue reference but is V, the Roman five; 'Cooked' shuffles V plus VIABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bivalve is a mollusc with a hinged two-part shell, such as an oyster or mussel.

indicators.note: in places the counties abbreviation inside the tens word

parts.note: tens is the plural of ten
Northern Ireland is made up of six counties, abbreviated NI

explanation.surface: A game played across six counties in groups of ten.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6 down but refers to Northern Ireland's six counties.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, a ball game.

clue.text: Bird with an exceptionally large figure

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird with an unusually large build.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a giant, from the mythological race of huge gods.

indicators.note: of the signals the answer is taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: The colour of a blade's sharp edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters lie across 'cutTING Edge'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight shade or tint of a colour.

clue.text: Be cautious about a trainee bounder's procession

indicators.note: about means the caution word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: cave is Latin for beware, school slang for watch out
L stands for learner, as on L-plates
a cad is a bounder

explanation.surface: A warning to be wary of a young rogue's parade.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE is Latin for 'beware', once schoolboy slang for a lookout's warning; L is the learner plate on a British trainee driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalcade is a procession, originally of riders on horseback.

clue.text: Best part of volcanic eruption keeps 4 friendly

indicators.note: keeps means the shuffled letters hold the four numeral inside
eruption suggests a violent breaking up, so the letters are rearranged
best part of means most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: Most of a volcanic eruption keeps four people on good terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best part of' drops the final C, leaving VOLCANI; 'eruption' shuffles that into CONVIAL, and 'keeps' holds the Roman four inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Convivial means sociable and genial, warmly friendly.

clue.text: Be in charge of fire again, dropping one note

indicators.note: dropping means the pieces for one and note are let fall from the end

parts.note: to reignite is to set on fire again
I is the Roman numeral for one
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone in charge relights a fire but misses one note.
explanation.walkthrough: From REIGNITE, the final ITE (I plus TE) drops away.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule, holding sovereign power over a realm.

clue.text: Go green, recycling source of yoghurt

indicators.note: recycling suggests something reprocessed, so the letters are made anew
source of means the first letter of the yoghurt word

explanation.surface: An eco slogan urging people to recycle their yoghurt pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb but is the noun meaning vigour; 'recycling' shuffles GREEN into ENERG, and 'source of' adds yoghurt's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Go means vigour or pep, as in full of go.

indicators.note: in places the woman's name inside the muddle word

parts.note: a mess is a muddle
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A thrifty woman is in a bit of a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanness is stinginess with money, the same as parsimony.
